title: Concurrent code you can test
hints: `new CompletableFuture<>()` is a result you complete yourself: inside the task run by the executor, call `complete(value)` or `completeExceptionally(error)`. An `Executor` has one method, `execute(Runnable task)`, so `executor.execute(() -> { ... })` hands it the work. Then `get()` on the futures in list order finds the first failure: for a failed future it throws an `ExecutionException`, whose `getCause()` is the original exception.
`AtomicLong.getAndSet(0)` reads and resets in one step, so no increment from another thread can slip in between.
rules: Make SafeCounter safe for many threads with AtomicLong, LongAdder or synchronized.
Run the tasks through the executor you are given.
